reference.source: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology / neuromuscular and myositis literature
clinicalPearls: Presents with subacute, severe, symmetrical proximal weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase
Defined serologically by anti-SRP or anti-HMGCR antibodies, though a seronegative form exists
Anti-HMGCR disease is associated with statin exposure and can persist or progress after the statin is stopped
Muscle biopsy shows scattered necrotic and regenerating fibres with sparse inflammatory infiltrate
Anti-SRP disease can be particularly aggressive and may involve cardiac and respiratory muscle
A paraneoplastic association exists, so age-appropriate malignancy screening is warranted
Treatment requires immunosuppression and, in statin-associated disease, permanent statin cessation
reference.pathophysiology: Immune-mediated necrotising myopathy is an autoimmune muscle disease in which antibodies against signal recognition particle or 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase are associated with ongoing muscle fibre necrosis. In anti-HMGCR disease, statin exposure is thought to up-regulate the target antigen and trigger an autoimmune response that continues independently of the drug. Complement deposition on muscle fibres and antibody-mediated injury drive prominent myofibre necrosis and regeneration with comparatively little lymphocytic infiltrate, distinguishing it histologically from the cell-mediated pattern of polymyositis and inclusion body myositis.
additionalDifferentials: Toxic or self-limited statin myotoxicity without autoimmunity
additionalInvestigations: Creatine kinase measurement, characteristically very high
Myositis-specific antibody testing for anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR
Muscle biopsy showing necrotic and regenerating fibres with minimal inflammation and complement deposition
MRI of muscle to demonstrate oedema and guide biopsy
Age-appropriate malignancy screening and cardiac and respiratory assessment in severe disease
redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness with respiratory or bulbar involvement
Cardiac involvement, particularly in anti-SRP disease
Persistent or worsening weakness despite stopping a statin
reference.prognosis: The disorder often requires prolonged immunosuppression and relapses are common, but many patients regain strength with treatment; anti-SRP disease tends to be more severe, and outcome worsens with cardiac or respiratory involvement or associated malignancy.
pitfalls: Assuming weakness will resolve simply by stopping the statin in anti-HMGCR disease
Mislabelling it as polymyositis and missing the necrotising pattern on biopsy
Failing to test for myositis-specific antibodies that define the subtype
Overlooking cardiac and respiratory muscle involvement or an occult malignancy
references: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
